To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) interference diversity can be exploited by event-based detection, (ii) the interference diversity gain depends on the number of interference sources, and (iii) the number of interference signals is unknown and must be estimated.

(1) the presence of interference in a single-user environment can cause SNR walls for detection of very weak primary signals; (2) the SNR wall problem can be mitigated by exploiting interference diversity across users; (3) to exploit this diversity, a shift in perspective from existence-based detection to event-based detection is needed; (4) the proposed approach is robust to unknown number and location of interference sources; and (5) it is also robust to unknown primary signal statistics.
